speaker: Andy Bell of Ride
sentence: I’ve taken on board a lot from David Roback’s guitar playing. It’s kind of Doorsy.

speaker: Brian Eno
sentence: It doesn’t have to be this person at the front with all the articulation and every word clear. It can just be a person in that mess and that was a real liberation for me.
citation: Brian Eno, choosing Glider by My Bloody Valentine for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "One of the things that I really love in that is the fact that there's singing in there but you have no idea what it's doing... that was a real liberation for me." He says the experience of hearing it "has a lot to do with what I'm doing now".

speaker: Brian Eno
sentence: When I heard this record I really thought that I’ve got to change what I’m doing. But the change was actually to do with recording practices as much as anything else.
citation: Brian Eno, choosing Court And Spark by Joni Mitchell for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "When I heard this record I really thought that I've got to change what I'm doing," the change being in recording practice, while making Another Green World.

citation: Stephen Morris of New Order, choosing Neu!'s Neu! for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "As a drummer, Klaus Dinger was important to me: [he taught me] how to make one riff last a lifetime!"

speaker: Stephen Morris of New Order
sentence: I used to make cassettes of Tago Mago and go and sit in a field – I don’t know why – to play it there in the middle of the night, because it seemed like the best way to listen to it. I wasn’t very old; 13 or 14, playing Tago Mago in a field on my own with a cassette player running out of battery.
citation: Stephen Morris of New Order, choosing Can's Tago Mago for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I used to make cassettes of Tago Mago and go and sit in a field... I wasn't very old; 13 or 14"
note: marginal: obsessive formative-years listening, nothing explicit about their own music

speaker: Mike Hadreas (Perfume Genius)
sentence: I count the cover as an influence. She’s defiant but not overt.
citation: Mike Hadreas (Perfume Genius), choosing Patti Smith's Horses for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I count the cover as an influence."

speaker: Britt Daniel of Spoon
sentence:
Is that heavy but still pop template something that inspired Spoon?

I think so.
citation: Britt Daniel of Spoon, asked for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen whether the heavy-but-pop template of Wipers's Over the Edge inspired Spoon: "I think so."

speaker: Jonathan Higgs of Everything Everything
sentence: But it was very shortly after we heard that that my friend got a drum kit and my brother got a guitar, and my brother had a bass, and I knew that all I had to do was pick up that bass and we had a band.
citation: Jonathan Higgs of Everything Everything, choosing Nirvana's Nevermind for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "it was very shortly after we heard that that my friend got a drum kit and my brother got a guitar... I knew that all I had to do was pick up that bass and we had a band"

speaker: Jamie Stewart of Xiu Xiu
sentence: When I was in 10th grade, I listened to ‘Kiss Me Kiss Me Kiss Me’ every single night before I went to bed for an entire year.
citation: Jamie Stewart of Xiu Xiu, choosing The Cure for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "When I was in 10th grade, I listened to 'Kiss Me Kiss Me Kiss Me' every single night before I went to bed for an entire year."
note: marginal: the 10th-grade line is about Kiss Me Kiss Me Kiss Me, not the picked compilation

speaker: Brix Smith Start (The Fall)
sentence: I think this is the album that made me want to play bass. It made me sit up and say, ‘I want to be in a band.’
citation: Brix Smith Start (The Fall), choosing Joy Division's Unknown Pleasures for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I think this is the album that made me want to play bass. It made me sit up and say, 'I want to be in a band.'"

speaker: Richard H. Kirk of Cabaret Voltaire
sentence: I was a Bowie fan from about 15. I went to see the Ziggy Stardust tour in Sheffield and was kind of blown away as much by the way he looked.
citation: Richard H. Kirk of Cabaret Voltaire, choosing David Bowie's Low for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I was a Bowie fan from about 15."
note: marginal: fan in formative years; Low itself is described as a turning point for electronic music

speaker: Steve Diggle of Buzzcocks
sentence: Bowie was an inspiration to [Buzzcocks] like The Beatles were.
citation: Steve Diggle of Buzzcocks, choosing David Bowie's 'Panic In Detroit' for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "Bowie was an inspiration to [Buzzcocks] like The Beatles were."

speaker: Stuart Murdoch of Belle and Sebastian
sentence: The Smiths were playing ‘Bigmouth Strikes Again’, and during the course of that song I became a different person.
citation: Stuart Murdoch of Belle and Sebastian, choosing The Smiths's The Queen Is Dead for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "during the course of that song I became a different person."

speaker: Stuart Murdoch of Belle and Sebastian
sentence: It had a great effect on me at the time, but I don’t listen to The Fall very often now. It went along with my abrasive nature at the time – this crazy ranter, Mark E Smith, appealed to me deeply.
citation: Stuart Murdoch of Belle and Sebastian, choosing The Fall's This Nation's Saving Grace for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "It had a great effect on me at the time, but I don't listen to The Fall very often now."
note: marginal: effect on him as a young listener, not on his songwriting

speaker: Johnny Marr of The Smiths
sentence: As a young guitar player, discovering 154 showed me a world that was an alternative way of looking at the instrument. It has stuck with me all the way through my career.
citation: Johnny Marr of The Smiths, choosing Wire's 154 for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "As a young guitar player, discovering 154 showed me a world that was an alternative way of looking at the instrument. It has stuck with me all the way through my career."

speaker: Johnny Marr of The Smiths
sentence: Buzzcocks influenced The Smiths massively in the way we approached our record sleeves and our choice of independent record company – because of the Buzzcocks we took on a Mancunian DIY ethic, whilst being in the charts.
citation: Johnny Marr of The Smiths, choosing Buzzcocks's Another Music In A Different Kitchen for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "Buzzcocks influenced The Smiths massively in the way we approached our record sleeves and our choice of independent record company"

speaker: Johnny Marr of The Smiths
sentence: with me being a teenager during the 70s meant I never stopped being affected by Brian’s music.
citation: Johnny Marr of The Smiths, choosing Brian Eno's Taking Tiger Mountain (By Strategy) for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "with me being a teenager during the 70s meant I never stopped being affected by Brian's music"
note: marginal: general effect of Eno's music on him as a teenager; the Taking Tiger Mountain remarks are about the record's reach

speaker: Dan Snaith of Caribou
sentence: People who know my albums from ten years ago will have heard me trying to rip off Silver Apples.
citation: Dan Snaith of Caribou, choosing Silver Apples' debut for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "People who know my albums from ten years ago will have heard me trying to rip off Silver Apples."

speaker: Michelle Zauner of Japanese Breakfast
sentence: When I started playing guitar, it was important for me to learn how to do finger-picking style because of those Elliott Smith records.
citation: Michelle Zauner of Japanese Breakfast, choosing Elliott Smith's XO for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "When I started playing guitar, it was important for me to learn how to do finger-picking style because of those Elliott Smith records."

speaker: Michelle Zauner of Japanese Breakfast
sentence: Musicians like her and Kimya Dawson had these very singular voices that were great for me. I loved their songwriting and the character in it and sort of gave me the courage to be a singer without sounding like Aretha Franklin or something.
citation: Michelle Zauner of Japanese Breakfast, choosing Joanna Newsom's Ys for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen, said Newsom's songwriting "sort of gave me the courage to be a singer without sounding like Aretha Franklin or something."

speaker: Michelle Zauner of Japanese Breakfast
sentence: My other big influence on [For Melancholy Brunettes (& Sad Women)] was Sufjan Stevens’ Carrie & Lowell.
citation: Michelle Zauner of Japanese Breakfast, choosing Sufjan Stevens' Carrie & Lowell for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "My other big influence on [For Melancholy Brunettes (& Sad Women)] was Sufjan Stevens' Carrie & Lowell."

speaker: Lol Tolhurst of The Cure
sentence: I’ve actually got part of a chapter in my new book about how Joe Strummer started me on this path.
citation: Lol Tolhurst of The Cure, choosing The Clash's debut for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I've actually got part of a chapter in my new book about how Joe Strummer started me on this path."

speaker: Lol Tolhurst of The Cure
sentence: What I always thought of with the drums was once the rhythm’s there, there’s this whole space inside of it that you can listen to and focus on with the push and pull. That’s what I was always trying for.
citation: Lol Tolhurst of The Cure, choosing Can's Tago Mago for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen, on Jaki Liebezeit's drumming: "there's this whole space inside of it that you can listen to and focus on with the push and pull. That's what I was always trying for."
note: Moderate: about drumming approach rather than the record itself; he also names Can alongside Cluster in his Low pick.

speaker: Joey Santiago of Pixies
sentence: That probably seeped in to [his and Black Francis’ playing] on ‘Monkey Gone To Heaven’ through osmosis.
citation: Joey Santiago of Pixies, choosing Television's Marquee Moon for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen, said its trading of rhythm and lead "probably seeped in" to his and Black Francis's playing on "Monkey Gone To Heaven" "through osmosis".
note: Hedged ('probably', 'we didn't mean it'); Marquee Moon was heard after Pixies had started. Owner may prefer favourite.

speaker: Mike Watt of Minutemen
sentence: When D’s mom makes us into a band and puts me on bass (I bought my first bass for $100), I had to learn bass from Fun House, Creedence and the brothers doing R&B, or like Trevor Bolder [of Bowie’s Spider From Mars and Uriah Heep], because you could really hear the bass on British rock & roll – most US rock & roll buried the bass in the mix.
citation: Mike Watt of Minutemen, choosing The Stooges' Fun House for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen, said that when he was put on bass, "I had to learn bass from Fun House, Creedence and the brothers doing R&B", and that Fun House was "a freak out moment for us" and "the lingua franca" of their scene.

speaker: Will Sergeant of Echo & the Bunnymen
sentence: I learnt all the wobbly guitar sounds you hear on the Bunnymen records from this. I’ve been living off that ever since, really.
citation: Will Sergeant of Echo & the Bunnymen, choosing Television's Marquee Moon for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I learnt all the wobbly guitar sounds you hear on the Bunnymen records from this. I've been living off that ever since, really."

speaker: Will Sergeant of Echo & the Bunnymen
sentence: And I thought, ‘right, I can kinda do that!’ And that’s when I started getting into recording, buying tape recorders and equipment, because I saw myself more as a creator than a guitarist.
citation: Will Sergeant of Echo & the Bunnymen, choosing Brian Eno's Another Green World for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen, on watching Eno with Roxy Music: "I thought, 'right, I can kinda do that!' And that's when I started getting into recording, buying tape recorders and equipment".

speaker: Alan Sparhawk of Low
sentence: I remember learning the chords to that song on the guitar, and that was the big lightning bolt going on.
citation: Alan Sparhawk of Low, choosing The Clash's Combat Rock for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen, on learning "Should I Stay Or Should I Go?": "I remember learning the chords to that song on the guitar, and that was the big lightning bolt going on."

speaker: Dallas Observer (on Jim Suptic)
sentence: Given the fact that his high school band, Kingpin, was heavily influenced by Slint, The Jesus Lizard and bands on the Amphetamine Reptile label, it comes as no surprise what show he saw first with his own money.
